result:
Admins can now rename their team from the profile page. I haven't run tests, lint, type checks or the app, as you asked, so none of it has been exercised yet.

- **API:** `features/teams/api/update-team.ts` adds the name schema, `updateTeam` (`PATCH /teams/{teamId}` with `{ name }`) and `useUpdateTeam`. On success the hook refreshes the teams list and shows a "Team Renamed" notification.
- **Mock API:** `PATCH /teams/:teamId` in `testing/mocks/handlers/teams.ts` returns 401 if you're not signed in. It rejects non-admins, and rejects an admin trying to rename a team other than their own with a 403. It then saves the change to the mock database.
- **UI:**
  - `UpdateTeam` is the Rename button and form drawer.
  - `TeamSection` shows the team name and wraps the button in `<Authorization allowedRoles={[ROLES.ADMIN]}>`.
  - `TeamSection` is added to the profile route below the user card.
- **Tests:** I added `app/routes/app/__tests__/profile.test.tsx`. It covers an admin renaming a team and a regular user not seeing the Rename button.

There is no endpoint for fetching a single team. `TeamSection` takes the user's team from the existing `/teams` list by matching `user.teamId`, so the name appears only once that list has loaded. A dedicated `GET /teams/{id}` would be cleaner if you add one to the mock contract.

The new mock handler's catch block uses `error: any`, as the existing handlers do. That is the only place the new code uses `any`.
